profile.reading:
This building near Water Street in Exeter, New Hampshire is identified as Phillips Exeter Academy's Information Technology Data Center. Phillips Exeter is a private secondary school founded in 1781, one of the oldest and most well known boarding schools in the United States, sitting on a roughly 700 acre campus in Exeter, in Rockingham County. Like the other academic and institutional entries in this registry, it is not a commercial data center operator, and this facility almost certainly exists to run the school's own administrative and instructional computing rather than to serve outside customers.

A secondary school's data center needs are modest by the standards of the commercial and hyperscale facilities that dominate this registry. Typical workloads for an institution like Exeter include student information and registrar systems, learning management and classroom technology, campus network and wireless infrastructure, library systems, dormitory and safety systems, email and administrative software, and backup and disaster recovery for those systems. Exeter's own published materials describe a curriculum with a computer science requirement and instructional technology investments over the years, which implies ongoing institutional investment in campus IT more broadly, though the school's public facing communications are aimed at prospective students and families rather than at documenting its facilities infrastructure, and none of the material reviewed for this entry describes the data center itself, its capacity, or its construction history.

No power capacity, square footage, year built or equipment detail specific to this building has been published by the school or identified in the sourcing behind this entry. That is unsurprising. Independent schools generally do not publicize their IT infrastructure, both because it holds little public interest compared to their academic programs and because unlike commercial operators they have no reason to market data hall capacity to prospective tenants. Rockingham County property and permit records would be the most direct path to specifics such as building square footage, year built or any addition history, but no such record specific to this address has been reviewed here. The most that can be said with confidence is that this is a small, campus scale enterprise IT facility serving one institution's own needs, built at a scale far below the multi megawatt commercial facilities found elsewhere in this registry, and that Exeter has not chosen to publish further detail about it.

reading:
Phillips Exeter Academy is a private boarding secondary school in Exeter, New Hampshire, at 20 Main Street. It describes a campus of about 700 acres including its woodlands, 26 dormitories and two dining halls, and a set of buildings unusual for a school at this level. The Class of 1945 Library, designed by Louis Kahn, holds more than 390,000 volumes and 210 study carrels and is described by the school as the largest secondary school library in the world. The Phelps Science Center holds 22 classroom laboratories. The Goel Center for Theater and Dance runs to 63,000 square feet. The Lamont Health and Wellness Center has fourteen beds and nurses on duty day and night. A residential school of that size runs student information systems, a learning management platform, a campus network reaching every dormitory, card access, telephony and health records, and that is the kind of institution this row represents.

What the registry actually holds is a single mapped building tagged as a data centre and named Information Technology Data Center, with Phillips Exeter Academy given as operator. The object carries no street address, no floor count, no year of construction and no floor area, and the registry stores its location only as Rockingham County. Its coordinates place it on the Water Street side of campus, roughly 200 metres north of the Academy Building, immediately beside Tattersall House at 237 Water Street, an academy owned residence dating to about 1732, and a short walk from the town's main sewer pumping station on the Squamscott River. In other words it is a small structure inside a dense historic campus block, not an isolated industrial site.

Beyond that, the public record is genuinely empty, and this page will not pretend otherwise. The academy's own campus and facilities pages name dozens of buildings down to individual dormitories and the boathouse and do not list this one. No square footage, rack count, contracted utility service, standby generation or critical IT load has been published by the school, and nothing surfaced in the Town of Exeter's planning record. This registry stores no capacity for the site and should not acquire one by inference. The name itself most likely came from a campus map label rather than from any description of scale.

That thinness is the point worth recording. The mapping tag that put this row in the registry draws no distinction between a 1.3 million square foot hyperscale campus and a single climate controlled room in a school building. A registry seeded from such tags will place the two side by side, and a facility count built on them will read a boarding school's server room as equivalent to a corporate campus unless the difference is written down. This page writes it down.
